questions.question_text: What will be the next term in the given series? 2, 13, 79, 475, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 6 and then increased by 1: 2×6+1=13, 13×6+1=79, and 79×6+1=475. Thus the next term is 475×6+1=2851.
questions.source: Series 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What number replaces the question mark? 2, 14, 70, 210, ?
questions.explanation: The multipliers descend through the odd numbers 7, 5, 3, 1: 2×7=14, 14×5=70, 70×3=210, so the next term is 210×1=210.
questions.source: Series 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the missing term? 3, 21, 147, ?, 7203
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 7. The missing term is 147×7=1029, and 1029×7=7203 confirms the continuation.
questions.source: Series 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 19; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 115, 102, 107, 94, 99, ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate −13 and +5: 115−13=102, 102+5=107, 107−13=94, and 94+5=99. Continue with 99−13=86.
questions.source: Series 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 20; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What replaces the question mark? 6, 5, 18, 10, 54, 20, ?, 40
questions.explanation: Separate odd and even positions. Odd-positioned terms 6,18,54 multiply by 3, so the missing term is 162. Even-positioned terms 5,10,20,40 double each time.
questions.source: Series 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 21; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 15, 8, 20, 18, 25, 28, ?
questions.explanation: Read odd and even positions separately. Odd-positioned terms 15,20,25 increase by 5, so the next is 30. Even-positioned terms 8,18,28 increase by 10.
questions.source: Series 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 22; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the ninth pair in the series? 3+3, 8+4, 15+5, 24+6, 35+7, ...
questions.explanation: Track the two components. The first is n(n+2), giving 99 at n=9; the second increases 3,4,5,6,7,... and is 11 at n=9. The ninth pair is 99+11.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 4; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Series 1 is 2, 8, 3, 27, 4, 64, 5, 125. Series 2 follows the same pattern: 11, α, β, γ, !, @. Find γ − α.
questions.explanation: Series 1 alternates n and n³. Applying the same pattern to Series 2 gives 11,11³,12,12³,..., so α=1331 and γ=1728. Therefore γ−α=1728−1331=397.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 5; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Series 1 is 712, 356, 178, 89. Series 2 follows the same pattern: 124, α, β, γ. Find 2(α − γ).
questions.explanation: Series 1 halves at each step. Apply the same rule to Series 2: α=62, β=31, and γ=15.5. Then 2(62−15.5)=93.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: The series is 2, 3, α, 15, 26, γ, 50. Find γ − α.
questions.explanation: Use consecutive squares alternately increased by 1 and decreased by 1: 1²+1=2, 2²−1=3, 3²+1=10, 4²−1=15, 5²+1=26, 6²−1=35, 7²+1=50. Thus γ−α=35−10=25.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In the series 5, 11, 18, (25), 35, (45), 56, decide whether the bracketed numbers are correct.

options.B: The first is correct and the second is incorrect.
options.C: The first is incorrect and the second is correct.

questions.explanation: The differences should be +6,+7,+8,+9,+10,+11, giving 5,11,18,26,35,45,56. The first bracketed value should be 26, so 25 is incorrect; the second bracketed value 45 is correct.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In the series 19, 23, 29, (31), (33), 41, decide whether the bracketed numbers are correct.

options.B: The first is correct and the second is incorrect.
options.C: The first is incorrect and the second is correct.

questions.explanation: The consecutive primes are 19,23,29,31,37,41. The first bracketed number, 31, is correct. The second should be 37, not 33, so it is incorrect.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What replaces the question mark? 52, 25, 04, 40, ?, 65
questions.explanation: The terms form adjacent digit-reversal pairs: 52,25; 04,40; 56,65. Since 65 is the reversal of 56, the missing term is 56.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What should replace the question mark? 6 + √216, 7 + √343, 8 + √512, 9 + √729, ?
questions.explanation: The integer before the plus sign increases by 1, and each radicand is its cube: 6³=216 through 9³=729. The next expression is 10+√(10³)=10+√1000.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What replaces the question mark? 1/√5, 2/5, 3/(5√5), 4/25, 5/(25√5), ?
questions.explanation: At position n, the numerator is n and the denominator is (√5)^n. The denominators are √5,5,5√5,25,25√5; the sixth term is 6/(√5)^6=6/125.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 10/1, 30/7, 60/13, 100/19, ?
questions.explanation: Treat numerator and denominator separately. Numerators increase by 20,30,40, then 50, giving 150. Denominators increase by 6, giving 25. The next fraction is 150/25.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 16; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two preceding terms. Since 34+55=89, the next term is 89.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 17; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 2/3, 4/7, 7/13, 11/21, ?
questions.explanation: Numerator increases are 2,3,4, so next add 5: 16. Denominator increases are 4,6,8, so next add 10: 31. The next fraction is 16/31.
questions.source: Series 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 19; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong term in the series: 2, 6, 24, 120, 420
questions.explanation: The terms multiply by consecutive integers: 2×3=6, 6×4=24, 24×5=120, so the next term should be 120×6=720. The printed 420 is incorrect.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 6, 6, 6, 8, 24, 28, 150
questions.explanation: The operations alternate adding an even number and multiplying by the next integer: +0, ×1, +2, ×3, +4, ×5. The last term should be 28×5=140, not 150.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 12, 60, 30, 150, 75, 376, 187.5
questions.explanation: The operations alternate ×5 and ÷2: 12×5=60, 60÷2=30, 30×5=150, 150÷2=75, 75×5=375, and 375÷2=187.5. Thus 376 is incorrect.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 11, 24, 39, 63, 525, 636
questions.explanation: Concatenate n with n² for n=1..6: 11,24,39,416,525,636. The fourth term should be 416, so 63 is wrong.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong term in the series: 17, 20, 24, 26, 29, 32, 35
questions.explanation: The intended series adds 3 each time: 17,20,23,26,29,32,35. The displayed 24 breaks this arithmetic progression and should be 23.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 180, 182, 186, 192, 198, 210
questions.explanation: The successive increases should be +2,+4,+6,+8,+10, producing 180,182,186,192,200,210. Thus 198 is wrong; the fifth term should be 200.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 5, 27, 61, 122, 213, 340, 509
questions.explanation: The terms follow n³−3 for n=2..8: 5,24,61,122,213,340,509. The displayed 27 is wrong; it should be 24.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 18; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 0, 1, 9, 36, 81, 225, 441
questions.explanation: These are squares of consecutive triangular numbers: 0²,1²,3²,6²,10²,15²,21², giving 0,1,9,36,100,225,441. Thus 81 is wrong and should be 100.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 21; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Find the wrong number in the series: 0, 4, 18, 48, 96, 180
questions.explanation: The terms follow n³−n² for n=1..6: 0,4,18,48,100,180. The fifth term should be 5³−5²=100, so 96 is wrong.
questions.source: Series 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 3; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: What is the next alphanumeric term? A1, C4, F9, J16, O25, ?
questions.explanation: Letter positions increase by 2,3,4,5, then 6: A,C,F,J,O,U. The number component is 1²,2²,3²,4²,5², then 6²=36. The next term is U36.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 5, 8, 7, 13, ?
questions.explanation: Separate odd and even positions. Odd positions form Fibonacci numbers 2,3,5,8,13. Even positions form consecutive primes 2,3,5,7, so the next even-positioned term is 11.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: What is the next term? 1, 4, 10, 20, 35, 56, ?
questions.explanation: The first differences are 3,6,10,15,21, consecutive triangular numbers. The next difference is 28, so the next term is 56+28=84.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: What is the next term in the series? 1, 2, 5, 12, 29, ?
questions.explanation: From the third term onward, each term is twice the previous term plus the term before it: 1, 2, 2×2+1=5, 2×5+2=12, and 2×12+5=29. Therefore the next term is 2×29+12=70.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Find the next term: 3, 4, 7, 16, 43, ?
questions.explanation: The successive differences are 1, 3, 9, and 27. These differences multiply by 3 each time, so the next difference is 81. Add it to the last term: 43+81=124.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question
